A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same KOALA++ research. Their complete main texts, equations, tables, figures, and appendices are readable and support reliable matching across additions, moves, and renumbering.

before.justification: Section 4 and Appendices B–D report original KOALA++ classification, language-modeling, eigenvalue-tracking, and ablation results.

after.justification: Original experimental results remain, with additional gradient-alignment, Muon convergence, and computational-efficiency evaluations in Appendices C and E.

M1.justification: Section 3 and Algorithm 1 retain the same gradient-covariance recursion, symmetric and asymmetric variants, parameter update, and initialization. Renaming variables and newly explaining noise estimation do not establish an algorithm change. PSD-enforcing modifications remain future work.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate image classification on CIFAR-10, CIFAR-100, and ImageNet32, plus language modeling on WikiText-2. The additional analyses retain this coverage; Swin-Base extends model scale rather than dataset or task coverage.

E2.justification: v2 adds Muon to the CIFAR-10 convergence comparison alongside SGD and Adam in Appendix C.2/Figure 5. Existing accuracy-comparison baseline sets remain, including Shampoo; the new efficiency comparisons largely reuse previously evaluated optimizers.

E3.justification: v2 adds gradient-angle monitoring, a 100-epoch cosine-schedule convergence comparison, and substantial efficiency protocols: runtime and peak-memory profiling across architectures, batch sizes 256 and 1024, and a 128–1024 batch-size sweep. Section 4.1 also restricts the stated two-stage 200-epoch decay modification to CIFAR-10, whereas v1 described it for CIFAR-10/100 collectively.

E4.justification: New Appendix C investigates directional positivity across three datasets and early versus late convergence relative to Muon. Appendix E.3 adds resource-scaling analyses, including batch-dependent overhead against SGD. The original eigenvalue tracking and batch-size, scheduler, and initialization ablations remain; their relocation is not an addition.

E5.justification: Uncertainty reporting expands to the main CIFAR comparison in Table 2, which changes from point estimates to entries with standard deviations. A new footnote reports rerunning earlier benchmark-derived results. v1 already documented three-seed experiments and five-seed statistics in Table 4, so this does not establish an increased seed count.

E6.justification: Many Table 2 estimates change: CIFAR-10/ResNet-18 at 200 epochs changes from SGD/KOALA++ errors of 5.61/5.41 to 4.83/5.43, reversing their ranking. Table 3 revises both KOALA rows, and Table 5 changes AdaFisherW perplexity from 153.99 to 152.72. Figures 4–5 and Tables 10–12 add alignment, convergence, and efficiency results. These are revised estimates and new evaluations of the retained algorithm.

T1.justification: Appendix C.1 adds an effective update-matrix formulation and reasoning connecting H_k v_k^T > 0 to positivity along the current gradient direction (Equations 63–65). The original minimum-norm and eigenvalue derivations remain mathematically equivalent apart from notation. No global PSD or convergence proof is added.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same central contributions: structured uncertainty propagation through compact gradient-covariance products, minimum-norm covariance approximation, and competitive vision/language performance with first-order-like efficiency. Additional evidence and wording changes do not redefine these claims.

C2.justification: v2 newly distinguishes the fitted covariance surrogate from the recursive update matrix and interprets gradient alignment as effective PSD behavior. It also hypothesizes why KOALA++ initially fluctuates more than Muon and explains shrinking runtime overhead with larger batches. These substantially extend the mechanism discussion, while formal PSD and convergence guarantees remain unresolved.

D1.justification: v2 supplies a KOALA++ repository link and states that code and configurations are public. Appendix E.2.1 newly documents online measurement-noise estimation using an exponential moving average with smoothing factor 0.9 and clarifies process-noise selection. Detailed vision runtime and memory costs are also added; the hardware and most existing training hyperparameters remain unchanged.

R1.justification: Section 2.2 substantially expands positioning against low-rank Bayesian/EKF approaches and SLANG through observation-model and complexity comparisons. References to Chang, Duran-Martin, SLANG, and Muon are added, while the de Vilmarest and Takenga references are removed.

P1.justification: The main section sequence and most exposition remain intact. v2 shortens the title, edits language and notation, rewrites portions of related work, and reorganizes the appendices around added sections and a conference checklist.

P2.justification: v2 adds two multipanel analysis figures and three efficiency tables. Existing displays are also revised, including explanatory labels in Table 1, uncertainty subscripts in Table 2, and distinct best/second-best highlighting. All nine original plot figures are retained, with renumbering and relocation where needed.

improvement.justification: Rerun results with uncertainty in Table 2, runtime/memory evidence in Tables 10–12, and implementation/access disclosures make the central empirical claims easier to assess and reproduce. However, Appendix C.1 overstates directional positivity as evidence of full-matrix PSD, and Figure 4 labels angles in radians while the text interprets degrees. The empirical documentation improves, but the new stability argument does not resolve the original theoretical limitation.
